name: Blackberry Sauce
headnote: Wilemon's headnote is a single thin line: an easy blackberry sauce meant for cheesecake, ice cream or even pancakes, served warm over vanilla ice cream or cold over plain cheesecake. There is no technique discussion at all on the page beyond the method itself, which simmers the berries with sugar and brandy before thickening with a cornstarch slurry.
comment_digest: The top review (84 helpful, SUNSETINAZ) passes on a family trick: drop in about 8 peppercorns before cooking and strain them out with the seeds afterwards, which adds a layer of flavour without reading as peppery. That tip is echoed by many later reviewers and is effectively the recipe's best-known amendment. Straining is the second theme, with several saying the blackberry seeds make the sauce unpleasant to eat and one suggesting you hold back a few whole berries to stir in after straining. Sugar is worth tasting down: one reviewer needed only half the cup with sweet berries, another added more when the berries were sour. Many increase the brandy or add an extra spoonful after cooking, since much of it boils off. Substitutions reported as successful include bourbon, Jack Daniel's, rum, Grand Marnier, kirsch, apple brandy and Framboise, as well as frozen berries and mixed berries (blueberry, raspberry), with the water reduced slightly for frozen fruit.
flags: Manifest name is 'Blackberry Sauce' but the page is titled 'Sweet Blackberry and Brandy Sauce'; manifest name kept as instructed.
